root.title: Offer Ready
root.note: A connected, proactive TCU student-to-career companion. Product concept, not an implemented integration.

children.title: Understand the student
children.note: Connect context, ask better questions, and keep the student in control.

children.title: People & pain points
children.note: Who the concept serves and the problems the team described.

children.title: Current TCU students
children.note: Students across years and majors; a freshman finance major is the recurring example. The initial pilot audience is still open.

children.title: Unclear career direction
children.note: Students may not know what jobs involve, what interests them, or how their current activities relate to future roles.

children.title: Fragmented information
children.note: Academic plans, career advice, job listings, campus opportunities, calendars, and application materials live in different places.

children.title: Missing or unsuitable openings
children.note: The user reports seeing about three Textron internships on Handshake but more on the employer website, and difficulty finding quant roles. These are student observations, not a verified market-wide comparison.

children.title: Eligibility mismatches
children.note: Students want to avoid spending time on roles they cannot take because of stated requirements, year, location, or authorization.

children.title: Generic communication
children.note: The team finds many existing recommendation emails irrelevant and wants a more useful, individualized experience.

children.title: Application strain
children.note: Repeated research and tailoring take time; the discussion links this burden to application burnout.

children.title: Authenticity gap
children.note: Students may write what they think employers want instead of communicating their actual experience honestly.

children.title: Connected accounts
children.note: Proposed authorized connections. No live API access or institutional agreement has been verified.

children.title: TCU school profile
children.note: Prefill major, year, academic context, and other approved student information rather than asking students to re-enter everything.

children.title: Stellic & academic planning
children.note: Use permitted degree progress, completed/planned courses, and relevant advising information where the connected system actually provides it. Do not assume Stellic owns all appointment records.

children.title: Advising appointment records
children.note: Connect the appropriate authorized school appointment system so the assistant can identify recorded past or upcoming meetings.

children.title: Outlook calendar
children.note: Use authorized class/calendar information to suggest suitable times and coordinate approved appointments and invites.

children.title: LinkedIn & Handshake
children.note: Proposed profile connections for career context. Public-job discovery and private-account access are separate; availability and permissions remain unverified.

children.title: GitHub & other profiles
children.note: Use student-approved projects and portfolio information where relevant to the goal.

children.title: Connection health & fallback
children.note: Show what is connected, when it was synced, and what could not be read. Offer uploads or manual correction if a connection is unavailable.

children.title: Access is not completeness
children.note: Connections reduce uncertainty, but a failed sync or unrecorded meeting is not proof an event never happened. Ask when coverage is incomplete.

children.title: Contextual onboarding
children.note: Start from available information, then ask questions that genuinely clarify the student.

children.title: Import before interviewing
children.note: Connect approved apps, extract available information, then ask personalized follow-up questions.

children.title: Clarify the person
children.note: Explore interests, aspirations, concerns, preferred work, and what the student enjoyed or disliked about past experiences.

children.title: Confirm personal contribution
children.note: Clarify what the student actually did in projects, clubs, volunteering, and work before turning it into application claims.

children.title: Editable profile & goals
children.note: Keep current goals, constraints, and confirmed experience on the profile; let the student correct them.

children.title: No assumed answers
children.note: Distinguish imported records, student-confirmed facts, AI interpretations, and missing information.

children.title: Preferences & boundaries
children.note: Make personalization explicit instead of opaque.

children.title: Year, major & experience
children.note: Adapt guidance for freshmen, sophomores, juniors, seniors, majors, and experience level.

children.title: Hard constraints vs preferences
children.note: Separate cannot-relocate or explicit role requirements from preferences such as remote work, industry, or commute.

children.title: Weighting & customization
children.note: Let students influence ranking and see why recommendations change; the board calls for strong filtering and weighting.

children.title: Nationality wording
children.note: The board mentions nationality. Recommended refinement: ask relevant optional work-authorization or sponsorship questions, not nationality-based judgments.

children.title: Unknown eligibility
children.note: Do not mark unclear requirements as confirmed eligibility or ineligibility; present the uncertainty and an official clarification route.

children.title: Plan a personal path
children.note: Connect academic choices, campus activity, skill-building, and career exploration.

children.title: Career exploration
children.note: Help students investigate possibilities without declaring a fixed life path.

children.title: Questions before conclusions
children.note: Use a series of questions to explore the student’s interests and possible directions.

children.title: Explain roles plainly
children.note: Show future job titles, what people do day to day, relevant industries, positions, possible paths, and source-supported pay information where available.

children.title: Optional exploration tasks
children.note: Suggest activities or small experiments students can try before committing to a direction.

children.title: Forecasting & uncertainty
children.note: Some forecasting was proposed. Label scenarios as exploratory rather than guarantees about future jobs, pay, or the student’s life.

children.title: Human skills & curiosity
children.note: Emphasize authentic experience, human judgment, curiosity, and willingness to test tools.

children.title: JobsGPT inspiration
children.note: Mentor reference: break careers into tasks and explore how AI may affect work; use this to discuss skills and future possibilities, not to guarantee outcomes.

children.title: Academic roadmap
children.note: The team’s broader vision includes semester-level academic planning.

children.title: Semester-by-semester classes
children.note: For example, show a finance major which courses fit each semester, using appropriate requirements and available information.

children.title: What each class teaches
children.note: Explain course learning and how it could relate to skills, projects, and careers.

children.title: Progress & dependencies
children.note: Use completed/planned courses and check prerequisites, sequencing, requirements, and known offering information.

children.title: Requirements vs suggestions
children.note: Separate official graduation rules from elective or career recommendations; use current authoritative sources and catalog context.

children.title: Academic advisor review
children.note: Refer exceptions, substitutions, uncertain requirements, and official decisions to the appropriate advisor. Do not claim graduation clearance.

children.title: Prototype vs full vision
children.note: Decide how much academic planning belongs in the Offer Ready demonstration versus a later phase; it overlaps the separate advising case.

children.title: Campus & skill opportunities
children.note: Make better use of the student’s time at TCU.

children.title: Relevant clubs
children.note: Recommend campus organizations related to interests and career goals, including meaningful activities to try as a freshman.

children.title: Certifications
children.note: Suggest relevant certifications with a reason, effort/cost where known, and no assumption that every credential is worthwhile.

children.title: Projects & portfolio
children.note: Recommend practical experiences that build genuine evidence for a skill gap; never label an unfinished project as completed experience.

children.title: Career fairs & networking
children.note: The discussion proposes a dedicated calendar for fairs and networking events, with preparation time.

children.title: Actionable details
children.note: Explain what the opportunity offers, the next step, and whether information is current.

children.title: Community connections
children.note: The board proposes community finding/connections. Exact function and whether this is a directory, peer support, or networking remain open.

children.title: Goals & adaptive milestones
children.note: Translate possibilities into actions the student can understand.

children.title: Profile-based goals
children.note: Show personal goals and next steps such as a career-advising conversation.

children.title: Near and long-term steps
children.note: The discussion proposes month-by-month or year-by-year milestones connected to a larger roadmap.

children.title: Dynamic focus system
children.note: A dynamic focus system is written on the board; exact behavior still needs definition.

children.title: Revisit the path
children.note: Adjust as classes, interests, constraints, advisor input, and experiences change.

children.title: Student ownership
children.note: Recommended: distinguish optional suggestions from student-approved commitments; allow changes without framing exploration as failure.

children.title: Find & pursue opportunities
children.note: Connect real openings to suitable students and complete the required application workflow.

children.title: Discovery beyond one board
children.note: Search suitable public sources rather than promise complete coverage.

children.title: Employer career pages
children.note: Find opportunities directly from companies, addressing the team’s Textron example.

children.title: Specialized opportunities
children.note: Support interests such as quantitative finance that the team feels are poorly served by its current search.

children.title: Jobs, internships & campus work
children.note: Cover roles, internships, and an identifiable TCU work-study category.

children.title: Freshness & provenance
children.note: Store source URLs and check times, deduplicate, and verify availability before calling a role current.

children.title: Public access boundaries
children.note: The case uses public postings; no unauthorized private Handshake, LinkedIn, or university scraping.

children.title: Coverage honesty
children.note: Say which sources and fields are supported; do not promise every job on the internet.

children.title: Explainable matching
children.note: Show what fits, what does not, and what still needs checking.

children.title: Role & personal priorities
children.note: Match interests, background, location, timing, compensation preferences, and other student-selected factors.

children.title: Year & graduation requirements
children.note: Respect clearly stated freshman/sophomore/junior/senior or graduation-window requirements.

children.title: Authorization & sponsorship
children.note: Use the actual posting and student-provided relevant information; distinguish work authorization, sponsorship, and citizenship requirements.

children.title: Strongest Match
children.note: For each shortlisted opening, identify the clearest fit between the student’s actual background and the posting.

children.title: Fit reasons & gaps
children.note: Separate required from preferred qualifications and explain important gaps instead of hiding them in a percentage.

children.title: No hiring guarantees
children.note: Internal fit scores are not employer ratings or probabilities of interviews/offers.

children.title: Authentic applications
children.note: Keep application preparation central to the selected case.

children.title: Resume/CV personalization
children.note: Tailor real experience to a role; the board includes ATS considerations.

children.title: Three resume versions
children.note: Use one sample student and base resume to produce at least three tailored resumes for three real openings.

children.title: Three cover letters
children.note: Create a genuinely tailored letter for each of the same three openings and flag student-specific details still needed.

children.title: Visible change comparison
children.note: Show original and revised wording, linked to the relevant line in each job posting.

children.title: Unsupported-claim check
children.note: Flag experience, tools, dates, accomplishments, or qualifications not supported by the resume or student input.

children.title: Evidence & student voice
children.note: Recommended: connect important wording to confirmed experience, preserve voice, and let the student approve/reject changes.

children.title: ATS-readable output
children.note: Use clear headings and standard formatting without problematic tables/graphics; no promise of an ATS pass.

children.title: Interview defensibility
children.note: Optional extension: help the student explain the experiences behind the strongest application claims.

children.title: Application bots & tracking
children.note: Clarify what the automation actually does.

children.title: “Bots sorting out TCU applications”
children.note: User’s phrase retained. Define whether it means research, organization, tailoring, tracking, or something else.

children.title: Organized status & follow-up
children.note: A lightweight record of roles, document versions, deadlines, and next actions was discussed as useful.

children.title: Student approval boundary
children.note: Recommended: preview and approve outbound messages, bookings, calendar invitations, and application submissions.

children.title: No false submitted status
children.note: Generating documents does not mean an application has been sent.

children.title: Support, act & learn
children.note: Proactive human support, connected records, and communication the student controls.

children.title: Advisors & follow-through
children.note: Support rather than replace career and academic professionals.

children.title: Contextual advisor referral
children.note: Suggest a career-advisor meeting when relevant to the student’s goals or uncertainty.

children.title: Read recorded meetings
children.note: Use authorized school appointment records and calendars to reduce repeated questions about past/upcoming meetings.

children.title: Schedule-aware offer
children.note: “Would you like me to help book a meeting around your class schedule?”

children.title: Booking & calendar invite
children.note: Proposed assistance with appointment selection and calendar invitations; access, availability, and approval remain implementation dependencies.

children.title: Meeting log into action
children.note: Use a permitted meeting log or student-approved summary to update goals and support decisions and optional tasks.

children.title: Summary verification
children.note: Recommended: confirm the summary with the student before treating interpreted advice as a commitment. Do not assume permission to record.

children.title: Notification choices
children.note: Latest user clarification: ask at account creation and explain the full proposed set.

children.title: Choose at onboarding
children.note: AI asks what notifications the student wants when the account is created.

children.title: Transparent defaults
children.note: Show all notification types the assistant proposes to send unless disabled; do not conceal categories behind vague personalization.

children.title: Turn off or adjust
children.note: Student can disable unwanted categories at setup or later.

children.title: Tailored emails
children.note: Messages should reflect that student’s relevant goals and situation, not generic or irrelevant job-email volume.

children.title: Calendar & deadline reminders
children.note: Potential categories include advisor meetings, roadmap tasks, applications, and campus events; the exact default list is not yet agreed.

children.title: Advance event notice
children.note: The audio proposes weeks of notice for fairs/networking rather than last-minute discovery.

children.title: Frequency & channel settings
children.note: Recommended extension: let students choose digest frequency, email/push/calendar channels, and quiet periods.

children.title: Personal feedback loop
children.note: Use corrections and progress to improve this student’s guidance.

children.title: Store preferences & corrections
children.note: Remember why the student rejected a job, changed a goal, or corrected an application claim.

children.title: Learn from activity carefully
children.note: Use completed tasks and confirmed advisor input to adjust next steps; do not assume clicks reveal a settled career goal.

children.title: Qualitative feedback
children.note: The board calls for qualitative feedback and continued testing with students.

children.title: Not deterministic life advice
children.note: Present options, trade-offs, and uncertainty while keeping student and advisor judgment involved.

children.title: Efficient research reuse
children.note: Preserve the board’s “inner feedback loop” idea without mixing private identities.

children.title: Store past public pulls
children.note: Save reusable public research and extractions so similar searches use less repeated work/tokens.

children.title: Personalized finishing step
children.note: Adapt current research to the individual student instead of blindly replaying a prior output.

children.title: Cache vs learning
children.note: Public caching saves effort; changing guidance from student feedback is a separate mechanism.

children.title: Protect private information
children.note: Keep resumes, personal constraints, advisor notes, and personalized drafts isolated with appropriate permissions.

children.title: Refresh stale material
children.note: Recheck job availability and time-sensitive campus information before recommending it.

children.title: Purpose, proof & delivery
children.note: Keep the full vision, the competition minimum, and unconfirmed ideas distinct.

children.title: Draft purpose statements
children.note: Consultant-written statements synthesized from the team’s direction; editable, not assumed approved.

children.title: Problem statement
children.note: Students lack a connected, personalized view of how their academic choices, campus experiences, eligibility, and career opportunities fit together, leaving them unsure what to pursue and what to do next.

children.title: Mission statement
children.note: Help TCU students turn their individual background, academic journey, and interests into informed career decisions and practical next steps through connected information, authentic AI guidance, and human support.

children.title: Vision statement
children.note: Every student can understand their options, make purposeful use of their time at TCU, and adapt their path as their interests and opportunities change.

children.title: Product goal
children.note: Create a student-controlled career companion that connects authorized academic and career information, asks relevant questions, and helps students explore, prepare for, and pursue suitable opportunities.

children.title: Student promise
children.note: Know your options. Understand your next step. Build a path that is yours.

children.title: Positioning
children.note: A connected student-to-career guide, not just another job feed: understand the student, connect preparation to opportunities, and support action and follow-through.

children.title: Values & intended outcomes
children.note: What the experience should stand for.

children.title: Authenticity
children.note: Honest, specific representation of the student’s own experience.

children.title: Human agency
children.note: Help students decide, question, explore, and act; do not prescribe their life.

children.title: Curiosity & experimentation
children.note: Encourage learning by trying tools, tasks, and opportunities.

children.title: Connected clarity
children.note: Explain why a course, activity, advisor meeting, or role matters to the student.

children.title: Privacy & transparency
children.note: Explain sources, permissions, uncertainties, and notification behavior.

children.title: Useful progress
children.note: Proposed north-star measure: students completing a self-approved, relevant career action with enough understanding to explain why it helps. Test application preparation time, unsupported claims, recommendation relevance, and student clarity; do not claim hiring gains without follow-up.

children.title: Competition deliverables
children.note: The wider vision does not replace the Offer Ready minimum.

children.title: One sample student
children.note: Use a real permitted resume or realistic stand-in profile with a target role/field.

children.title: Public current shortlist
children.note: Capture title, company, location, 3–5 key qualifications/keywords, and Strongest Match.

children.title: Three application pairs
children.note: Three tailored resumes plus three matching cover letters, with posting-linked before/after comparisons.

children.title: Honesty & ATS checks
children.note: Flag unsupported claims, preserve truthful qualifications, and provide standard ATS-readable formats.

children.title: Reusable AI build
children.note: Prompt template, skill, custom assistant, no-code workflow, or another reusable build. A one-off conversation does not count.

children.title: AI log & observed error
children.note: Document tools, workflow, and an actual confidently wrong AI output caught and corrected by the team.

children.title: Pitch deck & appendix
children.note: Include shortlist, three pairs, comparisons, and AI log; confirm current demo-video and upload logistics with organizers.

children.title: Judging rubric
children.note: Seven equal categories: innovation, technical execution, responsible AI, completeness, usability, impact, presentation. Attached rubric totals 28; some cases inconsistently mention 100.

children.title: Build, test & differentiate
children.note: Keep hypotheses separate from demonstrated results.

children.title: Working tool choice
children.note: “Replit?” appears on the board as a possible build environment, not a confirmed choice.

children.title: Desktop & phone usability
children.note: Good interface on computer and phone, with readable generated documents.

children.title: Team roles & roadmap
children.note: Board tasks include naming the product, assigning roles, defining the problem/audience, implementation roadmap, and feedback collection.

children.title: Test one complete journey
children.note: Recommended: demonstrate a student’s context → relevant next action → application → follow-through, rather than disconnected feature demos.

children.title: Measure a useful improvement
children.note: Proposed tests: relevance, student clarity, time including corrections, claim accuracy, and ability to explain application wording.

children.title: No unsupported superiority claim
children.note: Feature overlap with Handshake/LinkedIn does not prove equivalent experience. Claim better results only for the actual workflow and baseline tested.

children.title: Prioritization still open
children.note: Select what is live, clearly simulated, or future vision. Preserve all ideas without pretending the entire ecosystem can be built in one sprint.

children.title: Unresolved & parked ideas
children.note: Retained for completeness, not silently converted into product commitments.

children.title: Integration feasibility
children.note: Confirm authorized data sources, APIs, institutional permission, sync completeness, and advisor availability.

children.title: Forecasting evidence
children.note: Decide what forecasts mean, what sources support them, and how uncertainty is explained.

children.title: Task urgency & autonomy
children.note: Define optional tasks, deadlines, approval requirements, and how strongly the assistant nudges.

children.title: Community & dynamic focus
children.note: Specify these board terms before treating them as build requirements.

children.title: Employer-side marketplace
children.note: Audio discussion considered employer recruitment features and pushed toward student-facing focus. Retained as a parked discussion, not a confirmed build requirement.

children.title: Aggregated-data monetization
children.note: Audio discussion mentioned selling aggregated/anonymized demand/skill data. No approved business model, permissions, or privacy assessment was established. Do not implement from this note.

children.title: Naming & business model
children.note: Offer Ready is the current case/working label. Final name and sustainable business model remain open.

items.note: Make better use of the student’s time at TCU.

items.path: Offer Ready / Plan a personal path / Campus & skill opportunities / Relevant clubs
items.title: Relevant clubs
items.note: Recommend campus organizations related to interests and career goals, including meaningful activities to try as a freshman.

items.path: Offer Ready / Plan a personal path / Campus & skill opportunities / Certifications
items.title: Certifications
items.note: Suggest relevant certifications with a reason, effort/cost where known, and no assumption that every credential is worthwhile.

items.path: Offer Ready / Plan a personal path / Campus & skill opportunities / Projects & portfolio
items.title: Projects & portfolio
items.note: Recommend practical experiences that build genuine evidence for a skill gap; never label an unfinished project as completed experience.

items.path: Offer Ready / Plan a personal path / Campus & skill opportunities / Career fairs & networking
items.title: Career fairs & networking
items.note: The discussion proposes a dedicated calendar for fairs and networking events, with preparation time.

items.path: Offer Ready / Plan a personal path / Campus & skill opportunities / Actionable details
items.title: Actionable details
items.note: Explain what the opportunity offers, the next step, and whether information is current.

items.path: Offer Ready / Plan a personal path / Campus & skill opportunities / Community connections
items.title: Community connections
items.note: The board proposes community finding/connections. Exact function and whether this is a directory, peer support, or networking remain open.

items.path: Offer Ready / Plan a personal path / Goals & adaptive milestones
items.title: Goals & adaptive milestones
items.note: Translate possibilities into actions the student can understand.

items.path: Offer Ready / Plan a personal path / Goals & adaptive milestones / Profile-based goals
items.title: Profile-based goals
items.note: Show personal goals and next steps such as a career-advising conversation.

items.path: Offer Ready / Plan a personal path / Goals & adaptive milestones / Near and long-term steps
items.title: Near and long-term steps
items.note: The discussion proposes month-by-month or year-by-year milestones connected to a larger roadmap.

items.path: Offer Ready / Plan a personal path / Goals & adaptive milestones / Dynamic focus system
items.title: Dynamic focus system
items.note: A dynamic focus system is written on the board; exact behavior still needs definition.

items.path: Offer Ready / Plan a personal path / Goals & adaptive milestones / Revisit the path
items.title: Revisit the path
items.note: Adjust as classes, interests, constraints, advisor input, and experiences change.

items.path: Offer Ready / Plan a personal path / Goals & adaptive milestones / Student ownership
items.title: Student ownership
items.note: Recommended: distinguish optional suggestions from student-approved commitments; allow changes without framing exploration as failure.

items.path: Offer Ready / Find & pursue opportunities
items.title: Find & pursue opportunities
items.note: Connect real openings to suitable students and complete the required application workflow.

items.path: Offer Ready / Find & pursue opportunities / Discovery beyond one board
items.title: Discovery beyond one board
items.note: Search suitable public sources rather than promise complete coverage.

items.path: Offer Ready / Find & pursue opportunities / Discovery beyond one board / Employer career pages
items.title: Employer career pages
items.note: Find opportunities directly from companies, addressing the team’s Textron example.

items.path: Offer Ready / Find & pursue opportunities / Discovery beyond one board / Specialized opportunities
items.title: Specialized opportunities
items.note: Support interests such as quantitative finance that the team feels are poorly served by its current search.

items.path: Offer Ready / Find & pursue opportunities / Discovery beyond one board / Jobs, internships & campus work
items.title: Jobs, internships & campus work
items.note: Cover roles, internships, and an identifiable TCU work-study category.

items.path: Offer Ready / Find & pursue opportunities / Discovery beyond one board / Freshness & provenance
items.title: Freshness & provenance
items.note: Store source URLs and check times, deduplicate, and verify availability before calling a role current.

items.path: Offer Ready / Find & pursue opportunities / Discovery beyond one board / Public access boundaries
items.title: Public access boundaries
items.note: The case uses public postings; no unauthorized private Handshake, LinkedIn, or university scraping.

items.path: Offer Ready / Find & pursue opportunities / Discovery beyond one board / Coverage honesty
items.title: Coverage honesty
items.note: Say which sources and fields are supported; do not promise every job on the internet.

items.path: Offer Ready / Find & pursue opportunities / Explainable matching
items.title: Explainable matching
items.note: Show what fits, what does not, and what still needs checking.

items.path: Offer Ready / Find & pursue opportunities / Explainable matching / Role & personal priorities
items.title: Role & personal priorities
items.note: Match interests, background, location, timing, compensation preferences, and other student-selected factors.

items.path: Offer Ready / Find & pursue opportunities / Explainable matching / Year & graduation requirements
items.title: Year & graduation requirements
items.note: Respect clearly stated freshman/sophomore/junior/senior or graduation-window requirements.

items.path: Offer Ready / Find & pursue opportunities / Explainable matching / Authorization & sponsorship
items.title: Authorization & sponsorship
items.note: Use the actual posting and student-provided relevant information; distinguish work authorization, sponsorship, and citizenship requirements.

items.path: Offer Ready / Find & pursue opportunities / Explainable matching / Strongest Match
items.title: Strongest Match
items.note: For each shortlisted opening, identify the clearest fit between the student’s actual background and the posting.

items.path: Offer Ready / Find & pursue opportunities / Explainable matching / Fit reasons & gaps
items.title: Fit reasons & gaps
items.note: Separate required from preferred qualifications and explain important gaps instead of hiding them in a percentage.

items.path: Offer Ready / Find & pursue opportunities / Explainable matching / No hiring guarantees
items.title: No hiring guarantees
items.note: Internal fit scores are not employer ratings or probabilities of interviews/offers.

items.path: Offer Ready / Find & pursue opportunities / Authentic applications
items.title: Authentic applications
items.note: Keep application preparation central to the selected case.

items.path: Offer Ready / Find & pursue opportunities / Authentic applications / Resume/CV personalization
items.title: Resume/CV personalization
items.note: Tailor real experience to a role; the board includes ATS considerations.

items.path: Offer Ready / Find & pursue opportunities / Authentic applications / Three resume versions
items.title: Three resume versions
items.note: Use one sample student and base resume to produce at least three tailored resumes for three real openings.

items.path: Offer Ready / Find & pursue opportunities / Authentic applications / Three cover letters
items.title: Three cover letters
items.note: Create a genuinely tailored letter for each of the same three openings and flag student-specific details still needed.

items.path: Offer Ready / Find & pursue opportunities / Authentic applications / Visible change comparison
items.title: Visible change comparison
items.note: Show original and revised wording, linked to the relevant line in each job posting.

items.path: Offer Ready / Find & pursue opportunities / Authentic applications / Unsupported-claim check
items.title: Unsupported-claim check
items.note: Flag experience, tools, dates, accomplishments, or qualifications not supported by the resume or student input.

items.path: Offer Ready / Find & pursue opportunities / Authentic applications / Evidence & student voice
items.title: Evidence & student voice
items.note: Recommended: connect important wording to confirmed experience, preserve voice, and let the student approve/reject changes.

items.path: Offer Ready / Find & pursue opportunities / Authentic applications / ATS-readable output
items.title: ATS-readable output
items.note: Use clear headings and standard formatting without problematic tables/graphics; no promise of an ATS pass.

items.path: Offer Ready / Find & pursue opportunities / Authentic applications / Interview defensibility
items.title: Interview defensibility
items.note: Optional extension: help the student explain the experiences behind the strongest application claims.

items.path: Offer Ready / Find & pursue opportunities / Application bots & tracking
items.title: Application bots & tracking
items.note: Clarify what the automation actually does.

items.path: Offer Ready / Find & pursue opportunities / Application bots & tracking / “Bots sorting out TCU applications”
items.title: “Bots sorting out TCU applications”
items.note: User’s phrase retained. Define whether it means research, organization, tailoring, tracking, or something else.

items.path: Offer Ready / Find & pursue opportunities / Application bots & tracking / Organized status & follow-up
items.title: Organized status & follow-up
items.note: A lightweight record of roles, document versions, deadlines, and next actions was discussed as useful.

items.path: Offer Ready / Find & pursue opportunities / Application bots & tracking / Student approval boundary
items.title: Student approval boundary
items.note: Recommended: preview and approve outbound messages, bookings, calendar invitations, and application submissions.

items.path: Offer Ready / Find & pursue opportunities / Application bots & tracking / No false submitted status
items.title: No false submitted status
items.note: Generating documents does not mean an application has been sent.

items.path: Offer Ready / Support, act & learn
items.title: Support, act & learn
items.note: Proactive human support, connected records, and communication the student controls.

items.path: Offer Ready / Support, act & learn / Advisors & follow-through
items.title: Advisors & follow-through
items.note: Support rather than replace career and academic professionals.

items.path: Offer Ready / Support, act & learn / Advisors & follow-through / Contextual advisor referral
items.title: Contextual advisor referral
items.note: Suggest a career-advisor meeting when relevant to the student’s goals or uncertainty.

items.path: Offer Ready / Support, act & learn / Advisors & follow-through / Read recorded meetings
items.title: Read recorded meetings
items.note: Use authorized school appointment records and calendars to reduce repeated questions about past/upcoming meetings.

items.path: Offer Ready / Support, act & learn / Advisors & follow-through / Schedule-aware offer
items.title: Schedule-aware offer
items.note: “Would you like me to help book a meeting around your class schedule?”

items.path: Offer Ready / Support, act & learn / Advisors & follow-through / Booking & calendar invite
items.title: Booking & calendar invite
items.note: Proposed assistance with appointment selection and calendar invitations; access, availability, and approval remain implementation dependencies.

items.path: Offer Ready / Support, act & learn / Advisors & follow-through / Meeting log into action
items.title: Meeting log into action
items.note: Use a permitted meeting log or student-approved summary to update goals and support decisions and optional tasks.

items.path: Offer Ready / Support, act & learn / Advisors & follow-through / Summary verification
items.title: Summary verification
items.note: Recommended: confirm the summary with the student before treating interpreted advice as a commitment. Do not assume permission to record.

items.path: Offer Ready / Support, act & learn / Notification choices
items.title: Notification choices
items.note: Latest user clarification: ask at account creation and explain the full proposed set.

items.path: Offer Ready / Support, act & learn / Notification choices / Choose at onboarding
items.title: Choose at onboarding
items.note: AI asks what notifications the student wants when the account is created.

items.path: Offer Ready / Support, act & learn / Notification choices / Transparent defaults
items.title: Transparent defaults
items.note: Show all notification types the assistant proposes to send unless disabled; do not conceal categories behind vague personalization.

items.path: Offer Ready / Support, act & learn / Notification choices / Turn off or adjust
items.title: Turn off or adjust
items.note: Student can disable unwanted categories at setup or later.

items.path: Offer Ready / Support, act & learn / Notification choices / Tailored emails
items.title: Tailored emails
items.note: Messages should reflect that student’s relevant goals and situation, not generic or irrelevant job-email volume.

items.path: Offer Ready / Support, act & learn / Notification choices / Calendar & deadline reminders
items.title: Calendar & deadline reminders
items.note: Potential categories include advisor meetings, roadmap tasks, applications, and campus events; the exact default list is not yet agreed.

items.path: Offer Ready / Support, act & learn / Notification choices / Advance event notice
items.title: Advance event notice
items.note: The audio proposes weeks of notice for fairs/networking rather than last-minute discovery.

items.path: Offer Ready / Support, act & learn / Notification choices / Frequency & channel settings
items.title: Frequency & channel settings
items.note: Recommended extension: let students choose digest frequency, email/push/calendar channels, and quiet periods.

items.path: Offer Ready / Support, act & learn / Personal feedback loop
items.title: Personal feedback loop
items.note: Use corrections and progress to improve this student’s guidance.

items.path: Offer Ready / Support, act & learn / Personal feedback loop / Store preferences & corrections
items.title: Store preferences & corrections
items.note: Remember why the student rejected a job, changed a goal, or corrected an application claim.

items.path: Offer Ready / Support, act & learn / Personal feedback loop / Learn from activity carefully
items.title: Learn from activity carefully
items.note: Use completed tasks and confirmed advisor input to adjust next steps; do not assume clicks reveal a settled career goal.

items.path: Offer Ready / Support, act & learn / Personal feedback loop / Qualitative feedback
items.title: Qualitative feedback
items.note: The board calls for qualitative feedback and continued testing with students.

items.path: Offer Ready / Support, act & learn / Personal feedback loop / Not deterministic life advice
items.title: Not deterministic life advice
items.note: Present options, trade-offs, and uncertainty while keeping student and advisor judgment involved.

items.path: Offer Ready / Support, act & learn / Efficient research reuse
items.title: Efficient research reuse
items.note: Preserve the board’s “inner feedback loop” idea without mixing private identities.

items.path: Offer Ready / Support, act & learn / Efficient research reuse / Store past public pulls
items.title: Store past public pulls
items.note: Save reusable public research and extractions so similar searches use less repeated work/tokens.

items.path: Offer Ready / Support, act & learn / Efficient research reuse / Personalized finishing step
items.title: Personalized finishing step
items.note: Adapt current research to the individual student instead of blindly replaying a prior output.

items.path: Offer Ready / Support, act & learn / Efficient research reuse / Cache vs learning
items.title: Cache vs learning
items.note: Public caching saves effort; changing guidance from student feedback is a separate mechanism.

items.path: Offer Ready / Support, act & learn / Efficient research reuse / Protect private information
items.title: Protect private information
items.note: Keep resumes, personal constraints, advisor notes, and personalized drafts isolated with appropriate permissions.

items.path: Offer Ready / Support, act & learn / Efficient research reuse / Refresh stale material
items.title: Refresh stale material
items.note: Recheck job availability and time-sensitive campus information before recommending it.

items.path: Offer Ready / Purpose, proof & delivery
items.title: Purpose, proof & delivery
items.note: Keep the full vision, the competition minimum, and unconfirmed ideas distinct.

items.path: Offer Ready / Purpose, proof & delivery / Draft purpose statements
items.title: Draft purpose statements
items.note: Consultant-written statements synthesized from the team’s direction; editable, not assumed approved.

items.path: Offer Ready / Purpose, proof & delivery / Draft purpose statements / Problem statement
items.title: Problem statement
items.note: Students lack a connected, personalized view of how their academic choices, campus experiences, eligibility, and career opportunities fit together, leaving them unsure what to pursue and what to do next.

items.path: Offer Ready / Purpose, proof & delivery / Draft purpose statements / Mission statement
items.title: Mission statement
items.note: Help TCU students turn their individual background, academic journey, and interests into informed career decisions and practical next steps through connected information, authentic AI guidance, and human support.

items.path: Offer Ready / Purpose, proof & delivery / Draft purpose statements / Vision statement
items.title: Vision statement
items.note: Every student can understand their options, make purposeful use of their time at TCU, and adapt their path as their interests and opportunities change.

items.path: Offer Ready / Purpose, proof & delivery / Draft purpose statements / Product goal
items.title: Product goal
items.note: Create a student-controlled career companion that connects authorized academic and career information, asks relevant questions, and helps students explore, prepare for, and pursue suitable opportunities.

items.path: Offer Ready / Purpose, proof & delivery / Draft purpose statements / Student promise
items.title: Student promise
items.note: Know your options. Understand your next step. Build a path that is yours.

items.path: Offer Ready / Purpose, proof & delivery / Draft purpose statements / Positioning
items.title: Positioning
items.note: A connected student-to-career guide, not just another job feed: understand the student, connect preparation to opportunities, and support action and follow-through.

items.path: Offer Ready / Purpose, proof & delivery / Values & intended outcomes
items.title: Values & intended outcomes
items.note: What the experience should stand for.

items.path: Offer Ready / Purpose, proof & delivery / Values & intended outcomes / Authenticity
items.title: Authenticity
items.note: Honest, specific representation of the student’s own experience.

items.path: Offer Ready / Purpose, proof & delivery / Values & intended outcomes / Human agency
items.title: Human agency
items.note: Help students decide, question, explore, and act; do not prescribe their life.

items.path: Offer Ready / Purpose, proof & delivery / Values & intended outcomes / Curiosity & experimentation
items.title: Curiosity & experimentation
items.note: Encourage learning by trying tools, tasks, and opportunities.

items.path: Offer Ready / Purpose, proof & delivery / Values & intended outcomes / Connected clarity
items.title: Connected clarity
items.note: Explain why a course, activity, advisor meeting, or role matters to the student.

items.path: Offer Ready / Purpose, proof & delivery / Values & intended outcomes / Privacy & transparency
items.title: Privacy & transparency
items.note: Explain sources, permissions, uncertainties, and notification behavior.

items.path: Offer Ready / Purpose, proof & delivery / Values & intended outcomes / Useful progress
items.title: Useful progress
items.note: Proposed north-star measure: students completing a self-approved, relevant career action with enough understanding to explain why it helps. Test application preparation time, unsupported claims, recommendation relevance, and student clarity; do not claim hiring gains without follow-up.

items.path: Offer Ready / Purpose, proof & delivery / Competition deliverables
items.title: Competition deliverables
items.note: The wider vision does not replace the Offer Ready minimum.

items.path: Offer Ready / Purpose, proof & delivery / Competition deliverables / One sample student
items.title: One sample student
items.note: Use a real permitted resume or realistic stand-in profile with a target role/field.

items.path: Offer Ready / Purpose, proof & delivery / Competition deliverables / Public current shortlist
items.title: Public current shortlist
items.note: Capture title, company, location, 3–5 key qualifications/keywords, and Strongest Match.

items.path: Offer Ready / Purpose, proof & delivery / Competition deliverables / Three application pairs
items.title: Three application pairs
items.note: Three tailored resumes plus three matching cover letters, with posting-linked before/after comparisons.

items.path: Offer Ready / Purpose, proof & delivery / Competition deliverables / Honesty & ATS checks
items.title: Honesty & ATS checks
items.note: Flag unsupported claims, preserve truthful qualifications, and provide standard ATS-readable formats.

items.path: Offer Ready / Purpose, proof & delivery / Competition deliverables / Reusable AI build
items.title: Reusable AI build
items.note: Prompt template, skill, custom assistant, no-code workflow, or another reusable build. A one-off conversation does not count.

items.path: Offer Ready / Purpose, proof & delivery / Competition deliverables / AI log & observed error
items.title: AI log & observed error
items.note: Document tools, workflow, and an actual confidently wrong AI output caught and corrected by the team.

items.path: Offer Ready / Purpose, proof & delivery / Competition deliverables / Pitch deck & appendix
items.title: Pitch deck & appendix
items.note: Include shortlist, three pairs, comparisons, and AI log; confirm current demo-video and upload logistics with organizers.

items.path: Offer Ready / Purpose, proof & delivery / Competition deliverables / Judging rubric
items.title: Judging rubric
items.note: Seven equal categories: innovation, technical execution, responsible AI, completeness, usability, impact, presentation. Attached rubric totals 28; some cases inconsistently mention 100.

items.path: Offer Ready / Purpose, proof & delivery / Build, test & differentiate
items.title: Build, test & differentiate
items.note: Keep hypotheses separate from demonstrated results.

items.path: Offer Ready / Purpose, proof & delivery / Build, test & differentiate / Working tool choice
items.title: Working tool choice
items.note: “Replit?” appears on the board as a possible build environment, not a confirmed choice.

items.path: Offer Ready / Purpose, proof & delivery / Build, test & differentiate / Desktop & phone usability
items.title: Desktop & phone usability
items.note: Good interface on computer and phone, with readable generated documents.

items.path: Offer Ready / Purpose, proof & delivery / Build, test & differentiate / Team roles & roadmap
items.title: Team roles & roadmap
items.note: Board tasks include naming the product, assigning roles, defining the problem/audience, implementation roadmap, and feedback collection.

items.path: Offer Ready / Purpose, proof & delivery / Build, test & differentiate / Test one complete journey
items.title: Test one complete journey
items.note: Recommended: demonstrate a student’s context → relevant next action → application → follow-through, rather than disconnected feature demos.

items.path: Offer Ready / Purpose, proof & delivery / Build, test & differentiate / Measure a useful improvement
items.title: Measure a useful improvement
items.note: Proposed tests: relevance, student clarity, time including corrections, claim accuracy, and ability to explain application wording.

items.path: Offer Ready / Purpose, proof & delivery / Build, test & differentiate / No unsupported superiority claim
items.title: No unsupported superiority claim
items.note: Feature overlap with Handshake/LinkedIn does not prove equivalent experience. Claim better results only for the actual workflow and baseline tested.

items.path: Offer Ready / Purpose, proof & delivery / Build, test & differentiate / Prioritization still open
items.title: Prioritization still open
items.note: Select what is live, clearly simulated, or future vision. Preserve all ideas without pretending the entire ecosystem can be built in one sprint.

items.path: Offer Ready / Purpose, proof & delivery / Unresolved & parked ideas
items.title: Unresolved & parked ideas
items.note: Retained for completeness, not silently converted into product commitments.

items.path: Offer Ready / Purpose, proof & delivery / Unresolved & parked ideas / Integration feasibility
items.title: Integration feasibility
items.note: Confirm authorized data sources, APIs, institutional permission, sync completeness, and advisor availability.

items.path: Offer Ready / Purpose, proof & delivery / Unresolved & parked ideas / Forecasting evidence
items.title: Forecasting evidence
items.note: Decide what forecasts mean, what sources support them, and how uncertainty is explained.

items.path: Offer Ready / Purpose, proof & delivery / Unresolved & parked ideas / Task urgency & autonomy
items.title: Task urgency & autonomy
items.note: Define optional tasks, deadlines, approval requirements, and how strongly the assistant nudges.

items.path: Offer Ready / Purpose, proof & delivery / Unresolved & parked ideas / Community & dynamic focus
items.title: Community & dynamic focus
items.note: Specify these board terms before treating them as build requirements.

items.path: Offer Ready / Purpose, proof & delivery / Unresolved & parked ideas / Employer-side marketplace
items.title: Employer-side marketplace
items.note: Audio discussion considered employer recruitment features and pushed toward student-facing focus. Retained as a parked discussion, not a confirmed build requirement.

items.path: Offer Ready / Purpose, proof & delivery / Unresolved & parked ideas / Aggregated-data monetization
items.title: Aggregated-data monetization
items.note: Audio discussion mentioned selling aggregated/anonymized demand/skill data. No approved business model, permissions, or privacy assessment was established. Do not implement from this note.

items.path: Offer Ready / Purpose, proof & delivery / Unresolved & parked ideas / Naming & business model
items.title: Naming & business model
items.note: Offer Ready is the current case/working label. Final name and sustainable business model remain open.
